The background tasks view always shows the current status, duration, and captured output for every task you've launched.
Failed status means the task ended with an error or a non-zero exit code.
Failed is the most likely explanation for a task that stopped unexpectedly.
For a failed task, you can read the output and error to see what went wrong.
Aborted status means the task was stopped before it finished.
For an aborted task, any output captured up to that point is discarded, so you can't see how far it got.
Completed status means the task finished cleanly: a command exited successfully, or a subagent returned its result.
For a completed task, you can read its full, final output.
In every case, the captured output stays readable in the background tasks view.
Finished, failed, and aborted tasks can be cleared from the background tasks view for a clean list.
A notification confirms when tasks are cleared.
A command that writes files, such as a build emitting artifacts, may have stopped partway, so you should check that it left things in an acceptable state.

A page called "How It Works" describes the mental model behind 100xprompt
You describe an outcome and 100xprompt reads your codebase, forms a plan, uses real tools to make changes, checks its own work, and asks before doing anything sensitive
At the core is a loop, modeled on how a careful engineer works
Understand step: it reads the relevant code before touching anything
Plan step: it breaks the request into steps, with a visible checklist for larger tasks
Act step: it edits files, runs commands, and searches code
Check step: it inspects every result and self-corrects, for example a failing test, a typo, or a missing import
Finish step: it summarizes what changed
Work happens inside a session, one thread holding the conversation, the changes, and the plan
Within a session you don't have to re-explain what you're building
You don't need this knowledge to be productive
Understanding it helps you steer it and get better results on long tasks
